beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a ready-mix concrete plant.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, the contractor bids, and the lowest quote wins a Letter of Acceptance. The contractor must then deposit a performance guarantee.

The company's major customers are all government or PSU entities: Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd.
This customer concentration is a key dependency: Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book, and the top customers accounted for 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018.

The company claims competitive strengths including long-standing client relationships (Western Railway since 2006), use of modern techniques like box pushing, a state-of-the-art RMC facility at Kashimira, Thane, and an experienced promoter team with over 20 years in the industry.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹8,661.35 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a compound decline of about 8.5% per year.
Net profit after adjustments shows volatility: it was ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, dropped to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then recovered sharply to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) was ₹784.46 lakhs in FY2014, peaked at ₹945.78 lakhs in FY2015, and was ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018.

Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹8,232.15 lakhs in FY2018. Long-term borrowings have declined from ₹586.63 lakhs to ₹133.09 lakhs over the same period, while short-term borrowings increased from ₹3,082.27 lakhs to ₹3,537.35 lakhs.
The company has acknowledged negative cash flows in recent financial years, though specific cash flow figures are not disclosed in the digest. This is flagged as a risk factor.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 7,495,476 equity shares — 90.949% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Other directors hold minimal shares: Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, and Mukesh Pandey each hold 300 equity shares.
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, aged 26, ACS). Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of equity shares.
Related-party transactions include loans taken from directors/officers (₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018), director remuneration (₹57.7 lakhs), and outstanding payables of ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.

Governance flags: Two companies promoted by the promoter (Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited) were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 for non-operation. The company issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price. No independent appraisal or monitoring agency has been appointed for the IPO.
Neither the promoter nor any director has been declared a willful defaulter by RBI, and there are no criminal cases against directors.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector in India is highly fragmented and working-capital-intensive, contributing around 8% to India's GDP.

Growth drivers include government flagship programs (100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, Power for All), eased FDI norms in construction, rising urbanization and disposable income, and a working-age population expected to reach 64% by 2021.

The market size: India's construction sector was valued at US$ 400 billion in 2015 and is projected to reach US$ 1,000 billion by 2025. The logistics sector is growing at a CAGR of 10.5% (US$ 160 billion in 2017 to US$ 215 billion by 2020).
Headwinds acknowledged by the company include the slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players in a fragmented market.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete (RMC) company that executes projects for government clients including Western Railway, Central Railway, MCGM, and MMRDA.
The company's business relies heavily on winning tenders from government departments, and its largest client, Indian Railways, contributed 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018.
This SME IPO is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares (₹10 face value). The proceeds are earmarked primarily for working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: identify A B Infrabuild as an infrastructure and RMC company based in Mumbai, its key clients (Indian Railways), and that it is raising funds for working capital via a fresh issue on the SME platform.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each. There is no offer for sale component. The issue price is to be determined through book building.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

The primary object of the issue is to meet working capital requirements, for which ₹1,130 lakhs (out of total proceeds to be determined) is earmarked. The balance is for general corporate purposes, the amount of which is not disclosed.
No independent agency has been appointed to appraise the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed — fund deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Indian Railways (via Western Railway) contributed 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018. Loss of this client would cause a significant revenue drop.
Negative cash flows: The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair its ability to meet obligations.
Related-party transactions: The company regularly transacts with related parties, including loans and payables, which may not be on arm's-length terms.
Unsecured loans repayable on demand: As of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans that are recallable at any time, creating liquidity pressure.
Promoter's struck-off companies: Two entities promoted by the promoter were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, raising governance concerns.
